preethi: Heads-up — kernel-selector canary rolled at 10:30. Seeing a host-side parse/tokenize CPU bump on canary nodes vs baseline. Attaching quick perf snapshot and numbers.

preethi: baseline p50/p95 host-parse: 120ms / 220ms
preethi: canary  p50/p95 host-parse: 140ms / 300ms :grimacing:

preethi: perf top (sampled):
```
 parse_tokenize      18% -> 35%
 grpc_unpack         12% -> 10%
 kv_cache_lookup     8%  -> 7%
 memcpy              2%  -> 14%
 ```

sam: Oof. memcpy went up a lot. Any idea which code path introduced the copies?

preethi: The selector started preferring the "fast_small_seq" kernel for seq_len < 64. That kernel expects contiguous input, so we added a preflight memcpy in host preparse to linearize framments. Code change is basically: `if (use_fast_kernel) memcpy(outbuf, fragments...)` — cheap for single large reqs but expensive at high QPS with many small requests.

anne: That lines up with the latency tail. Small chat prompts are now paying the copy cost on host before batching. Could we prefer the old kernel for HTTP/gRPC ingress or only enable fast_small_seq when input is already single-fragment?

devon: Also check KV cache churn: if copies change addresses we might hurt kvcache keying/halo. But perf numbers show memcpy is dominant here.

infra-bot: CI-bench summary for canary vs baseline:
- throughput: -2%
- host-parse CPU: +12%
- overall p95 latency: +30% on small-seq workload (chat-short)
- memory alloc rate: +9%

sam: Quick plan: 1) revert kernel-selector rule on canary (prefer old kernel for HTTP ingress) 2) run the microbench (small-seq chat) 3) consider changing kernel to accept fragmented inputs or move linearization into a sticky buffer reused across requests to avoid allocs.

preethi: Agreed. I'll push a revert candidate and a variant that gates memcpy behind "input_is_fragmented == false".

anne: If we gate by input shape, add a telemetry tag so we can see how often we actually hit the fast path.

preethi: Good call. I'll add metric tags: kernel_choice and preparse_copy=true/false.

devon: Also add a quick KV-check: run a kvcache-hit-rate diff; if keys differ we need to normalize before we change.

preethi: Will do. Revert PR is ready: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/2345 (canary rollback).

sam: Nice — once reverted, let's run the same perf snapshot and post numbers here. If regression disappears, we keep revert and iterate on kernel that avoids memcpy.

infra-bot: Deploy rollback completed to canary at 11:05 — monitoring.

preethi: Post-rollback numbers (11:20):
- host-parse p95 back to 225ms
- memcpy back down to 3% in perf sample
- overall p95 improved by ~26% vs bad canary

anne: :thumbsup: Marking this for follow-up: kernel selector redesign to be fragment-aware + add sticky buffer pool. Filing follow-up ticket: RTX-4821.

sam: Thanks everyone. Good catch and fast rollback.

preethi: I'll attach the perf flame and raw traces to the ticket.
